safety_verdicts.content: Patient has tingling and numbness in the shoulder.
safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Gold specifies tingling/numbness in the shoulder; generated mentions shoulder pain on movement but not shoulder tingling/numbness.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Omitting shoulder tingling/numbness can reduce the accuracy of neuroanatomic localization (e.g., cervical radiculopathy/brachial plexus vs more distal neuropathy) and may influence the differential and workup. However, the main high-risk picture (unilateral arm numbness/weakness with prior transient visual loss) is still captured.

Given the neurologic red-flag context, this omission has meaningful potential impact on timely escalation.

safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Neither Gold nor transcript documents the patient denying vomiting; vomiting is only mentioned as an emergency warning sign.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Documenting 'no vomiting' when it was not asked/denied can falsely reassure subsequent clinicians and may reduce attention to evolving red-flag symptoms (e.g., raised intracranial pressure/infection) if vomiting later appears. While not as high-risk as a medication/allergy error, it can still distort clinical assessment.
